title: Keeping Your Business Running Through a Disaster

body.en: You run a small tailoring business. A flood warning has just been issued for your area, and your workshop is on the ground floor. What's the most important business continuity step to take right now?

choices.label: Move your sewing machines, fabric stock, and financial records to higher ground immediately
choices.consequence: Right priority. For a small business, the equipment and stock often are the business — protecting them before the water arrives is what determines whether you reopen in days or in months.

choices.label: Keep working until the water actually reaches the door
choices.consequence: Too late by design. Waiting until the last moment risks losing equipment and stock you can't easily replace, and losing time you needed to move it safely.

choices.label: Assume insurance or savings will cover any losses, so no action is needed now
choices.consequence: Financial cover, if you have it, helps you recover — it doesn't prevent the disruption itself. Physically protecting your equipment now is what keeps the business running at all.
